people.role: Head of Vụ Ẩn Môn since 1146: mist formations and concealment arrays along the cape's roads
people.appearance: A thin, grey, unremarkable man in an oiled cloak, easy to forget even when he is standing in front of you, which he has practised.
people.backstory: Bàng Yên Tỏa was a tea-picker's son from Trà Viên Thôn, the tea village south of the sect's gate. At fifteen he was hired to carry loads on the cape roads. In 1100 the founder, Hàm Thủ Lộ (ham_thu_lo), saw him walk out of a robbers' ambush on the Phù Kiều road by keeping so still that nobody looked at him, and took him in. He learned the Road Mist Primer, then the Mist-Lock canon, then the Haze Walk that Tất Hành Vụ (tat_hanh_vu) had given the founder (N-thuy_vi-07). In 1146 the founder walked into his own mist by empty Đồng Sơn Trấn and was not found. Only his lantern was (N-vu_an-03). Bàng became head at sixty-one and has kept the sect small, quiet and paid. Its guards hold mist over the cape's roads for anyone who pays the road fee, and they do not ask who that is. Diêm Hải Tảo's (diem_hai_tao) carts use the roads, and so do people Thúy Vi would rather they did not. Tất still visits every spring. The Thúy Vi elders who call the walk a theft have begun to talk about a tithe.
people.wants: To keep Vụ Ẩn Môn out of every quarrel coming toward it: no tithe to Thúy Vi, no bargain with Tùng Đào, no robbers on his roads, and no one asking what is under the gate.
people.secret: The founder did not vanish. He died of old age in Bàng's arms on the Đồng Sơn road in 1146, at 198. He asked to be buried under the threshold of the seat's gate, and asked that the cape be told the mist had taken him, so that robbers would believe the mist could take a man. Bàng left the lantern burning on the road and carried the body home in mist. Hàm Thanh Đăng, the founder's daughter, believes her father was murdered.

people.appearance: A heavy, scarred man with a lynx-bone axe and a laugh that carries further than the mist he lays.
people.backstory: The fifth son of nobody, raised in the robbers' camp on the Ridge of the Bobtails. In 1081 a Thúy Vi road patrol ran him down on the Thạch Công road, and the founder Hàm Thủ Lộ (ham_thu_lo) hid him in mist and did not ask why (N-vu_an-02). He has guarded the road ever since. He formed his core in 1170, which puts him above his head in realm, and he will not take the headship: a robber can guard a road, he says, but not own one. In 1190 his old band killed his friend Bối Trường Đình (boi_truong_dinh) on the Đồng Sơn road.

people.appearance: A tall woman with ink-stained fingers who carries a green-paned lantern and looks at every stranger twice.
people.backstory: Hàm Thủ Lộ's (ham_thu_lo) daughter, born at the seat. She was forty-six when he walked into the mist by Đồng Sơn Trấn and was not found (N-vu_an-03). She keeps every crossroads lantern on the cape lit, and she keeps a ledger of everyone who has said in her hearing that the Haze Walk was stolen. She believes Thúy Vi's Hall of Rules took the art back in 1146 and her father with it. She calls Tất Hành Vụ uncle. She wants the founder's lantern from Bàng.

people.role: Mist-layer of the Phù Kiều road; on Tùng Đào's money
people.appearance: A neat woman in an undyed robe who smiles at everyone and remembers what they say.
people.backstory: Born in Phù Kiều Trấn, the river town the founder and Tất Hành Vụ (tat_hanh_vu) both came from. In 1192 her brother's gambling debts in Hàn Tân Thành were bought by an agent of Tùng Đào's first elder, Hồ Tùng Nguyệt (ho_tung_nguyet). The price of the debt is the Haze Walk's ninth layer. She does not have it. Only Tất can read it, and he trusts her because she is from his town.

people.role: Founder of Vụ Ẩn Môn (1050); the road guard who learned the Haze Walk
people.backstory: A carter's son from the river town of Phù Kiều Trấn and a road guard on the cape all his life. Tất Hành Vụ (tat_hanh_vu), eighteen years older, pulled him out of the river there as a boy, and they swore brotherhood when he came of age. In 1048 Tất taught him the Haze Walk (N-thuy_vi-07). He saw at once that mist laid like an array could hide a whole caravan, and he became a formation master at a hundred. In 1050 he founded Vụ Ẩn Môn to lay mist on the cape's roads and hide travellers from robbers (V015). He hid a robber once, in 1081, and never said why.
